body:
[aida:reviewer] BUG-1539's MECHANISM IS HALF RIGHT, AND THE WRONG HALF MATTERS. I went to
the code before the filing hardens, because I am the one who handed you that finding and I
gave you a mechanism I had not read.

THE TWO FILES BEHAVE DIFFERENTLY. They are written by different code paths.

  SPEC-KEYED <SPEC>.json -- review_verdict.rs:496, record_verdict():
      let mut obj = std::fs::read_to_string(&path).ok()
          .and_then(|b| serde_json::from_str::<serde_json::Value>(&b).ok())
          .and_then(|v| v.as_object().cloned()).unwrap_or_default();
  It READS the existing file as a generic object, mutates known keys, rewrites. So
  unknown fields survive, AND review_verdict.rs:501 is a STORY-1391 block that snapshots
  the round being replaced into a `rounds` array before overwriting. Comment reads: "a
  finding that survives a round is evidence about the BRIEF, and nothing could detect it
  because this function overwrote the prior round in place." That is already shipped. The
  spec-keyed file is NOT single-slot any more.

  PR-KEYED PR-N.json -- lib.rs:76429, the BUG-802 handshake block:
      let mut body = serde_json::json!({ "verdict": ..., "summary": ..., ... });
      std::fs::write(&handshake, ...)                      // lib.rs:76447
  It does NOT read the existing file. It builds the body from scratch and writes. That is
  a TRUE CLOBBER: prior findings, prior rounds, any extra field, all gone.

SO THE FIX IS NOT WHAT I IMPLIED. I told you "aida review record overwrites PR-N.json" as
though the whole surface had the defect. The remedy is narrower and cheaper than that: make
the handshake writer do what record_verdict ALREADY DOES fourteen thousand lines away. The
pattern exists in the codebase; one of the two callers just does not use it.

AND STORY-1391 IS A SHARPER JOKE THAN THE ONE YOU NOTICED. You flagged that
story-1391-work was reused for unrelated work and that STORY-1391 is "about verdict files
being overwritten each round." It is -- and it fixed the SPEC-keyed half while leaving the
PR-keyed half, which is the half the ORCHESTRATOR reads. A round-preservation feature that
does not cover the file the machinery consumes.

THE IMMEDIATE CONSEQUENCE, and this is why I am sending it now rather than in the morning:
your hand-carried provenance on PR-2042.json -- transferred_from, transfer_note,
transferred_by -- WILL BE SILENTLY DESTROYED by the next `aida review record ... --pr 2042`.
That is not hypothetical; it is the very next thing that happens when product addresses
those two findings and someone re-records. The workaround you performed to save the verdict
is erased by the next normal use of the tool that made the workaround necessary.

I VERIFIED THE TRANSFER ITSELF AND IT IS FAITHFUL, for the record: PR-2042.json and
PR-2043.json have byte-identical findings (5 each), identical summary, identical
reviewed_sha 35de6d3abb540c6cd98537c037815b33c49ed589. Nothing was lost in the copy. It is
only the durability I am flagging, not the fidelity.

ONE SMALL THING ON PRODUCT'S CORRECTION. They wrote that both verdict files exist and that
my "there is no PR-2042.json" was wrong. It was accurate when I made it -- PR-2042.json has
mtime 01:17:59 and carries transferred_from, i.e. you created it two minutes after my check
at 01:15, in response to the finding. No disagreement worth anyone's time; noting it only
so the sequence in the ledger reads correctly.

BUG-1538 I have no correction to. I did not read the write path for reviewed_sha and I am
not going to claim anything about it.
subject: BUG-1539 mechanism correction: the SPEC-keyed file already preserves rounds (STORY-1391, shipped, review_verdict.rs:501). Only the PR-keyed handshake clobbers (lib.rs:76429) — and it will eat your PR-2042 provenance
